cards.explanation: The answer is "My refuge and my fortress." The psalm writer says, “You are my refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.” (Psalm 91:2) A refuge is where you run to, and a fortress is walls around you. He's got a hiding place AND a wall, friends, and he's talking straight to the LORD about it.

The answer is True. Both are in verse 4: “under His wings you will find refuge; His faithfulness is a shield and rampart.” (Psalm 91:4) A rampart is a defensive wall. So you get two pictures, friends: wings to get under and a shield to stand behind.

The answer is False. The psalm says you will not fear “…the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day…” (Psalm 91:5) Then it keeps going with the pestilence in the darkness and the calamity at noon (Psalm 91:6). Night is just the first stop on a long list, friends.

The big picture is that there's no hour you need to fear. Look at the whole list, bakers: night terror, a daytime arrow, pestilence in the darkness, calamity at noon (Psalm 91:5-6). The psalm covers the dark hours AND the bright ones. It leaves no spot on the clock for fear.

The answer is True! Verse 7 says, “Though a thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, no harm will come near you.” (Psalm 91:7) Ten thousand! I can't keep track of ten thousand cookies on a cooling rack. Look at where the promise stands, friends: right in the middle of all those numbers, and it doesn't change.

The answer is "punishment." Verse 8 says, “You will only see it with your eyes and witness the punishment of the wicked.” (Psalm 91:8) So you watch it happen, and you only watch it. This is a heavy verse, friends, so I'll just stand quiet next to it for a second.

The reason is that you've made the LORD your home. Verse 9 says, “Because you have made the LORD your dwelling…” and then verse 10 says no evil will befall you. (Psalm 91:9-10) Dwelling means home, the place you live. The psalm ties the promise to where you've made your home, friends, and that home is the LORD.

The answer is "angels." Verse 11 says, “For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.” (Psalm 91:11) Notice who gives the command, bakers. It's God Himself, and the guarding covers all your ways.

The psalm says you will tread on them! Verse 13 says, “You will tread on the lion and cobra; you will trample the young lion and serpent.” (Psalm 91:13) Tread and trample, friends. Not tiptoe around. I'd pay good money to watch a lion find out about this verse.

The reason is that he loves the LORD. The LORD says, “Because he loves Me, I will deliver him…” (Psalm 91:14) The reason is love, plain and simple, friends. Nothing about being flawless or strong, just love.

The answer is True. There's a second reason in the same breath, friends. The LORD says, “because he knows My name, I will protect him.” (Psalm 91:14) So He gives one reason about love and one about knowing His name. Both are in verse 14.

The promise is that He'll be with him in it. The LORD says, “I will be with him in trouble.” (Psalm 91:15) Not just around it, friends, but with him in it. That might be my favorite line in the whole psalm.

The word is "salvation." The LORD ends the psalm with, “With long life I will satisfy him and show him My salvation.” (Psalm 91:16) It's the last thing He says, friends. That's a big note to finish on.
